summary: Jan Westerhoff works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at the University of Cambridge (~1995–2002) and SOAS, University of London (~2003–2005). He held posts at Durham University (attested 2011–2013) and the University of Oxford (~2012).

Jan Willem de Jong (1921–2000) was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He earned his Ph.D. at Leiden University (~1939–1949) and studied under Walter Eugene Clark and Paul Demiéville. He held chairs at Leiden (1956–1965) and ANU (from 1965).

Jan-Ulrich Sobisch specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under David P. Jackson, David Seyfort Ruegg, and Nubpa Rinpoche. His academic career includes posts at the Universities of Hamburg, Munich, and Copenhagen, where he was Prof. Dr. (2003–2006).

Jane Bunnag (born 1940) is a scholar in religious studies and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at the University of London by 1969, where she studied under supervisors E. Michael Mendelson and Barbara E. Ward.

Janet Gyatso is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She earned her Ph.D. at UC Berkeley (~1974–1981). Her career includes posts at Amherst College (attested 1990–2002) and Harvard University as Hershey Professor of Buddhist Studies (~2001).

Janet R. Goodwin works in Japanology, history/archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at UC Berkeley under Delmer M. Brown and Britten Dean. She has held posts at the University of Southern California and the University of Aizu (attested 1994).

Jang-Kil Chun is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. Chun completed doctoral studies under supervisor Minoru Kiyota and also studied under Paul J. Griffiths, Geshe Lhundub Sopa, and Frances A. Wilson.

Janice Dean Willis specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Tibetology. She studied at Cornell and earned her PhD at Columbia (~1971–1976) under Alex Wayman. She served as Professor at Wesleyan University (~1977–2014).

Jann Ronis specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from the University of Virginia, studying under David Germano, Jeffrey Hopkins, and Khenpo Sönam Tenpa, and held a post at the University of Virginia (attested 2007).

Jared Rhoton (1941–1993) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his dissertation at Columbia University by 1985 under doctoral supervisor Alex Wayman, and also studied under Sakya Trizin.

Jarl Charpentier (1884–1935) was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He earned his Ph.D. at Uppsala University (1902–1908) under Karl Ferdinand Johansson and studied at Bonn under Hermann Jacobi. He became Assistant Professor at Uppsala in 1908.

Jason Birch is an Indology and religious studies scholar. He completed a D.Phil. at Oxford (-2013) under Alexis Sanderson after studies at Sydney. He held posts at Oxford (attested 2011) and SOAS (attested 2020).

Jason Matthew McCombs is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned a B.S. at the University of Michigan and a PhD (-2014) at UCLA under Gregory Schopen, where he was also attested as a lecturer in 2014.

Jason Neelis works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He earned a PhD from the University of Washington (-2001) under Richard Salomon. His posts include Wilfrid Laurier University (attested 2013–2021) and Ruhr University Bochum (2009–2010).

Jason Protass works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned his PhD at Stanford University (attested 2015–2016) under John Kieschnick. He has held positions as a Fulbright Fellow at Academia Sinica and visiting researcher at Ryukoku University.

Jay Holt Valentine specializes in Tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Virginia under Kurtis R. Schaeffer, having previously studied at Naropa University and the University of Delaware (1992).

Jay Jasanoff (born 1942) is a linguist and Indologist. He studied at Harvard University (~1963–1968). He held academic posts at UC Berkeley (~1968–1972), Cornell University (~1978–1998), and Harvard University (~1998).

Jay L. Garfield works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Smith College (~1999), UMass Amherst (~1999), Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (~1999), Melbourne (~2007), and NUS (~2013–2016).

Jayandra Soni (born 1947) works in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He earned doctorates from Banaras Hindu University (~1974–1978) and McMaster University (~1978–1987). From ~1991 to 2012, he was a lecturer at the University of Marburg.
Jaś Elsner (born 1962) specializes in history, archaeology, and religious studies. He has held academic posts at the University of Michigan and at the University of Chicago (~2013).
